newsitem.title: USA: Banc One has long acquisition history.
newsitem.headline: Banc One has long acquisition history.

text.p: Banc One Corp, which on Monday proposed its highest-priced acquisition ever, has a long history of making and successfully integrating acquisitions.
Most of its 100-plus acquisitions over three decades were stock swaps that did not slow earnings momentum.
The Columbus, Ohio-based bank said it plans to acquire credit card issuer First USA Inc in a stock deal valued at $7.3 billion.
Banc One on Monday reported record 1996 earnings of $1.4 billion or $3.23 a share versus $1.3 billion or $2.91 in 1995. The stock was off 3-1/2 to 41-5/8 on the New York Exchange.
The 10th largest U.S. bank with assets of $101.8 billion at yearend, Banc One operates 1,502 branches in 12 states. It has said it wants to be a national financial services firm.
Formed in 1968 by the merger of two Ohio banks, by 1988 it had acquired about 60 well-run, small to mid-sized banks in Ohio and surrounding states and its assets placed it in the top 50 U.S. banks.

In 1989, Banc One stunned the industry by acquiring MCorp, a major Texas bank that had been seized by U.S. regulators. It was Banc One's largest acquisition to date with a price tag around $500 million, in an entirely new geographic market.
Through 1994, Banc One was on an acquisition tear, adding holdings in several states. Its 1992 acquisition of Arizona's Valley National Corp had a $1 billion-plus price tag.
"(Valley) turned out to be a financial home run," Joseph Duwan, an analyst with Keefe, Bruyette & Woods Inc, said.
In 1995 and 1996, Banc One was more often a bridesmaid than a bride, withdrawing its bid for Bank of Boston Corp and missing out on, or sitting out, several other major mergers.
In 1995 Banc One was reportedly asked to make a counteroffer for First Interstate when Wells Fargo was trying to acquire it. But nothing came of that.
Among other possible targets, it was reported that Banc One was a suitor for Boatmens but Banc One never confirmed or denied that.
In December, when it said it would buy Oklahoma's Liberty Bancorp in a stock swap valued at $546 million, analysts felt something bigger might be in the works.
Banc One said First USA will significantly change the way the bank competes in consumer financial services. It will double credit cardholders to 32 million.
First USA has $22.4 billion in managed receivables to Banc One's $12.6 billion.
The deal, due to close in May, is expected to dilute 1997 earnings by about seven percent but is not expected to reduce 1998 earnings, Banc One said.
Fred Cummings, an analyst with McDonald & Co, said he thinks the deal is a good long-term strategic move for Banc One but believes it will cut into earnings in 1997 and 1998.

But Duwan and analyst Kathryn Bissette of Sterne, Agee & Leach, said only 1997 should be affected. "Given the higher growth rate (of) revenues and earnings at First USA, they should be able to overcome the earnings dilution in a reasonable time," Bissette said.
Duwan said although there will be up-front earnings cost, "we feel they have increased the growth rate of the company on a longer term basis." He raised his rating to buy from hold.
((Cleveland Newsdesk 216-579-0077))
